key_insight: The paper introduces a least-squares weak Galerkin finite element framework that solves linear elasticity on general polytopal meshes with a symmetric positive definite formulation and no discrete inf-sup constraint.
engineering_relevance: This makes the method attractive for structural mechanics problems with complex geometry, irregular meshes, and nearly incompressible materials where locking and boundary-condition handling are challenging.
method: Uses weak differential operators: weak gradient, weak strain tensor, and weak divergence.
Formulates elasticity as a least-squares weak Galerkin method on weak finite element spaces.
Designed for polygonal/polyhedral meshes and robust treatment of boundary conditions and interfaces.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports optimal-order error estimates and extensive numerical experiments showing stability, efficiency, and locking-free performance in the nearly incompressible regime.
watch_item: Practical deployment may require careful construction of weak spaces and local operators to preserve stability and accuracy on highly irregular polytopal meshes.
paper_title: A Least Squares Weak Galerkin Framework for Linear Elasticity on Polytopal Meshes
